clue.text: World organisation's help withdrawn

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, with its possessive S kept as a letter
aid means help

explanation.surface: The United Nations has pulled its aid from a crisis zone.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that are withdrawn are retracted, as though they had never been spoken.

clue.text: Two ways one may have one's hair faulted

parts.words: Two ways one may have one's hair
parts.note: hair may be worn up, piled on the head

parts.words: Two ways one may have one's hair
parts.note: hair may also be braided, woven into plaits

explanation.surface: Two hairstyles, either of which might be criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: To upbraid is to scold or find fault with someone.

clue.text: Tube needed to be below the surface

definitions.text: Tube needed to be below the surface

parts.words: Tube needed to be below the surface
parts.note: the Tube suggests the London Underground, but this is a breathing pipe for a swimmer face-down in water

explanation.definitionFit: A swimmer breathes through this short curved pipe while floating face-down underwater.

clue.text: Girl Ernie ruined

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the name's letters are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: A young woman has been the ruin of a man called Ernie.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a girl's name, of Greek origin.

clue.text: A Bront taking wine may raise a flap here

parts.note: a Brontë: the three sisters published under the pseudonyms Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell (the accent is lost in the printed text)
tent is a deep red Spanish wine, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: One of the Brontë sisters gets tipsy and causes a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise a flap' suggests causing a fuss, but a tent's flap is lifted to go in. 'Taking' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A conical tent with a central pole has a door flap that campers lift to enter.

clue.text: A promising band

parts.note: band suggests a group of musicians with prospects, but it is a ring given with a promise to marry

explanation.definitionFit: This is a ring given when a couple pledge to marry, a band sealing a promise.

clue.text: It makes access difficult for part of hearing

definitions.meaning: a maze, a tangle of passages hard to get through
the inner ear, the organ of hearing and balance, is so called

explanation.definitionFit: A maze of passages is hard to penetrate, and the inner ear bears the same name.

clue.text: Squint to look at dungeon

parts.note: to eye is to look at
a hole is slang for a dungeon or prison cell, as in the black hole

explanation.surface: Peering cross-eyed into a prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squint' reads as a verb, but here it is a noun, a peephole.
explanation.definitionFit: A squint is an old word for a small opening or peephole to look through.

clue.text: City getting rid of an ass

indicators.note: the city name discards the two letters of the small word

parts.note: Antwerp is a port city in Belgium

explanation.surface: A town is clearing out its donkeys.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly fool, the same as calling someone an ass.

clue.text: Making lots from musical setting and presentation

parts.note: a mass is a musical setting of the Eucharist liturgy
a production is a staging or presentation of a show

explanation.surface: A big staging of a choral work.
explanation.definitionFit: Mass production is manufacturing goods in great quantities, making lots of them.

clue.text: British head sacked from Australian test site, having no good missile

indicators.note: the leading letter of the test site is dismissed and the British letter takes its post

parts.note: Woomera in South Australia is a rocket and weapons testing range

explanation.surface: A British boss is fired from a weapons range down under for his useless missile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head sacked' removes the W of WOOMERA and 'British' puts B in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved throwing stick of Aboriginal Australians is a hunting weapon hurled through the air.

clue.text: Note from vicar to remain outside

indicators.note: the remain word stands outside, so the vicar sits within it

parts.note: to be is to remain or continue, as in let it be
Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title

explanation.surface: A message from the clergyman asking someone to stay outside.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this is a long note worth two semibreves.

clue.text: Joint developing new leak

indicators.note: developing means taking new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pipe joint has sprung a fresh leak.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the joint linking the foot to the leg.

clue.text: Stripper in saccharine sort of opera

parts.note: saccharine means sugary, sweet as sugar
a soap opera is a serial drama, so soap is a sort of opera

explanation.surface: An exotic dancer appears in a syrupy musical drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stripper' suggests a dancer, but it means a cleaning agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar soap is an alkaline compound used to strip or clean paintwork before decorating.

clue.text: 4 .Obstetrician perhaps is a rounded .1 individual

definitions.meaning: an obstetrician delivers babies, so is a man who makes deliveries, by example
the stray .1 is an OCR artefact; a rounded individual is a roundsman, someone who makes a regular delivery round

explanation.definitionFit: Both a baby doctor and a roundsman bringing milk or parcels make deliveries.

clue.text: All around a length, maidens were played quietly

definitions.note: the definition describes the things, quiet instruments once played, rather than naming them

indicators.note: the maidens word goes all around the following pieces

parts.note: virgins are maidens

explanation.surface: Young women gathered at a distance and performed softly.
explanation.definitionFit: The virginals were small, soft-toned keyboard instruments popular in Tudor times.

clue.text: Organ requiring attention

definitions.meaning: to have someone's ... is to have their attention

explanation.definitionFit: The ear is the hearing organ, and lending an ear means paying attention.

clue.text: Turned up in fashionable eastern trousers

indicators.note: made into a new fashion, so the letters are restyled

explanation.surface: Someone arrives wearing stylish oriental trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like arrived, or a trouser hem, but means snub-nosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Retroussé describes a nose turned up at the tip.

clue.text: Obstruction causing injury with loss of time

indicators.note: the injury word loses the time word from within it

parts.note: damage is injury or harm
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A blockage that causes harm after time is wasted.
explanation.definitionFit: A dam is a barrier built across a river to hold back water.

clue.text: Order island fruit

parts.note: the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea
a date is the fruit of the date palm

explanation.surface: Instructions to fetch fruit from the island.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an authoritative command or order.

clue.text: Dress up in part of Yorkshire once by tradition

parts.note: Yorkshire was historically divided into three Ridings: North, East and West
a habit is a custom or tradition

explanation.surface: Putting on fancy dress in a corner of old Yorkshire, as custom dictates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress up' reads as putting on a costume, but here it is clothing worn when up on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the outfit worn for horse riding, clothing for someone mounted up in the saddle.

clue.text: Striker hating to be called out

definitions.text: Striker hating to be called out

parts.words: Striker hating to be called out
parts.note: a striker suggests a worker or footballer, but this one hits a ball in cricket and dreads the umpire's verdict of out

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the player at the crease strikes the ball and dreads being given out.

clue.text: One who brings round French wine during endless musical performance

indicators.note: the wine comes during the performance, so goes inside it
the performance word loses its final letter

parts.note: a concert is a musical performance
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: A man brings people round by pouring French wine through a never-ending gig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts the T from CONCERT, leaving CONCER, and VIN goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To convince someone is to bring them round to your view, so this is a persuader.

clue.text: Spiked instrument used in pits

parts.note: spiked and pits suggest a miner's tool, but it is a stringed instrument resting on an endpin and played in orchestra pits

explanation.definitionFit: This bowed string instrument stands on a metal endpin spike and is heard in theatre orchestra pits.

clue.text: Saw one had to check on vehicle ahead

indicators.note: the check goes in front of the other piece

parts.note: the MOT is the annual UK roadworthiness test for cars
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who saw a car had to get it inspected first.
explanation.walkthrough: MOT is the UK's compulsory annual vehicle safety test, named after the old Ministry of Transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, a synonym for a motto.

clue.text: Less than a mouthful for a walrus

indicators.note: the mouthful word falls a letter short, losing its last

parts.note: a morsel is a small bite, a mouthful of food

explanation.surface: A walrus would want more than a tiny bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse is an old word for the walrus, from Lappish.

clue.text: Load-carrier in a shopping precinct overturned

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, so in a down light the letters read backwards

parts.note: a mall is a shopping precinct

explanation.surface: A trolley loaded with goods tips over in a shopping centre.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American animal is used as a pack animal to carry loads in the Andes.

clue.text: One lacking knowledge of organ is kicked out of Musicians' Union

indicators.note: kicked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: MU is the abbreviation for the Musicians' Union

explanation.surface: An ignorant organist is expelled from the musicians' trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kicked out of' reads as expulsion, but it is the anagram signal for ORGAN, IS and MU together.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is a person who knows little, an uneducated or ignorant person.

clue.text: Curtsying is to be a new fashion

indicators.note: fashion as a verb means to shape or make, so the letters are formed anew

explanation.surface: Bobbing curtsies is about to become the latest trend.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisant means showing deference, such as by bowing or curtsying.

clue.text: Where to establish communication with the other side

definitions.text: Where to establish communication with the other side

parts.words: Where to establish communication with the other side
parts.note: the other side reads as the opposition or the far bank, but means the world of the dead, contacted at a spiritualist sitting

explanation.definitionFit: Spiritualists hold sittings in which a medium tries to contact the dead beyond the grave.
